shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A theophany announcement opens the unit, "כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ יָב֔וֹא" (oshb:Isa.66.15, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.15, 'for behold, Yahweh will come with fire'), rendered “For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire, and his chariots will be like the whirlwind” (web:Isa.66.15), a register shift from the maternal-comfort imagery of the preceding unit into universal judgment “on all flesh” (web:Isa.66.16). It closes at the indictment of those who eat forbidden food in the gardens, ending on the divine-speech signature "נְאֻם יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.17, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.17, 'says Yahweh'; this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed below). The unit ends there because 66:18 opens with a first-person emphatic pivot, “For I know their works and their thoughts.” (web:Isa.66.18), shifting the subject from judgment on apostates to the ingathering of the nations.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A koh-amar frame reopens the comfort oracle, "כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.66.12, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.12, 'for thus says Yahweh'), rendered “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream” (web:Isa.66.12). It develops the same nursing/comforting-mother imagery through “As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you.” (web:Isa.66.13) and closes at “Yahweh's hand will be known among his servants; and he will have indignation against his enemies.” (web:Isa.66.14). The unit ends there because 66:15 opens a new theophany announcement, “For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire” (web:Isa.66.15), a different register (judgment theophany rather than maternal comfort).

next_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a first-person emphatic pivot, “For I know their works and their thoughts. The time comes that I will gather all nations and languages” (web:Isa.66.18), moving the subject from judgment on apostates to a universal ingathering: survivors sent to far-off nations (66:19), all Israel's brothers brought as an offering (66:20), priests and Levites selected even from among them (66:21). It closes on a permanence assurance echoing the new-creation declaration of 65:17 as a lexical collocation differing in determination -- "שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.65.17, indefinite, byte tier) against "הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה" (oshb:Isa.66.22, definite, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.22, 'the new heavens and the new earth') -- each four-token run standing in exactly 1 verse book-wide, the two collating against each other at no tier. The postpositive pair "נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier) ('says Yahweh') stands mid-verse, at tokens 12-13 of 17, carrying the verse's own major dividing accent, with four further tokens -- "כֵּ֛ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם וְשִׁמְכֶֽם" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier) -- completing the comparison opened earlier in the same verse by "כִּ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר" (oshb:Isa.66.22, byte tier); it does not seal the unit. The unit ends there because 66:23 opens a new temporal formula ('from one new moon to another') describing recurring worship rather than the one-time ingathering event.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a recurring-time formula distinct from the one-time ingathering event of the preceding unit, “It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” (web:Isa.66.23), rendered in Hebrew as "יָב֧וֹא כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) ('all flesh will come to worship'), closing that same verse, “says Yahweh” (web:Isa.66.23), rendering "אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) -- a verse-final speech signature whose contiguous pair stands in 53 verses book-wide and verse-final in only 5 (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier), a byte fact this couplet's own held question weighs, not resolves. The book's very last verse turns from that universal worship to a grim closing image, “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched” (web:Isa.66.24), rendered "תוֹלַעְתָּ֞ם לֹ֣א תָמ֗וּת" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) ('their worm will not die'). This couplet is kept as its own unit because it is the book's terminal span (no rear seam follows 66:24) and because its own internal turn -- from universal worship to unending punishment of the transgressors -- is a distinct rhetorical function from the ingathering report that precedes it.

shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this couplet fused to the preceding ingathering unit as one larger span was considered, since no formal header or vocative separates 66:22 from 66:23, and 66:23 opens on a connective-prefixed temporal continuation, "וְהָיָ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier), attested verse-initially in 50 verses book-wide (sweep: 50 verses, skeleton tier) -- a form that distinguishes nothing at this seam by itself; it is rejected here because 66:23's recurring new-moon-and-Sabbath formula reports a standing liturgical order rather than continuing the one-time gathering narrated earlier in the chapter, a content distinction rather than a tier-1 form marker, which is why this row sits at reduced confidence rather than a higher band. Whether 66:24 functions as this oracle's own conclusion or as a coda to the whole book is held open from Isaiah's own text and not adjudicated here.

The all-flesh collocation itself spans the couplet and reaches beyond it: "כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר" (oshb:Isa.66.23, byte tier) stands inside this row's own first verse, "לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר" (oshb:Isa.66.24, byte tier) closes it verse-finally, and the chapter's third site stands at "כָּל בָּשָׂ֑ר" (oshb:Isa.66.16, byte tier) (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, 6 book-wide, skeleton tier) -- so the held coda-versus-close question carries byte evidence on both sides. This span closes the book; no rear seam follows Isa.66.24.
